content.text: Harry Styles just released his new album 'Kiss All The Time. Disco, Occasionally.' On 'Pop Culture Happy Hour,' host Stephen Thompson is joined by NPR Music's Hazel Cills and reporter Maria Sherman to discuss the album.⁠⁠🍸🔗 Hit the link in our bio to listen to the full episode.I feel like this could've been a lot less disappointing if he hadn't marketed it as disco or club anything.*Doing work on laptop music* is so real 😂 this album was such a letdownIf you don't hear dance in this album then you are tone deafJust because ‘disco’ is in the album title doesn’t mean the album is disco 😭 his just having fun with new sounds while keeping his essence intact.ITS like life of a showgirl. Good idea, but the music does not match.He’s not talented. Stop pushing himIt's a good album. People are overly critical about everything - if it isn't a series finale that isn't good enough, it is a sport/match that isn't good enough or an album that isn't good enough. For me, the album sounds good and is on repeat in myself household. 💪It's a real album kind of album. A real.... album albumI’m a Harrie for life but, definitely feel this is his weakest solo album to date. There are some awesome bangers but, a lot of generic musicIt’s a fantastic album. Makes you want to transcend while dancing.Let's not forget that one of his closest friends died tragically since Harry's House. To me, this album was about trying to find joy while you're grieving.I think if ppl stopped taking the album title as a literal nod to a genre, theyd appreciate it more. After listening to Harry’s interview with Tom Power, one realizes more Hs head-space while creating the new album. He matured personally and sonically. Im curious to see how that translates onstage. Very much enjoying KATTDO.Why do critics cut Harry Styles such slack while they attack other artists who release albums much more tightly put together than this one?If you think "Pop" and "Dance No More" are songs you'll just tap your feet to in a coffee shop, you need to get out more. Then again, this is NPR...I love it and can’t wait to let it sink in. It makes perfect sense with what he did this past three years just wondering around Europe, having fun and relaxing a bit. I’d love to hear the songs on the cutting room floor. Can’t wait to see it live.
